layout:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high fidelity 16:9 full-screen L5R Emperor Edition duel gameplay concept, 3840x2160 if possible.
Input images: Image 1 is the user's approved reference for LARGE UPRIGHT champion cards and sunset mood. Image 2 is the current native game, used for the existing dark navy mat, fine antique gold Japanese floral/wave border, five elemental emblems and crossed swords, crimson sunset landscape and restrained typography. Generate a new polished concept, not a comparison sheet.
Primary request: bring the mat much CLOSER to the player and make the real cards readable. Mat fills lower 72 percent of image, extends nearly to bottom edge with its entire front border visible and generous padding inside. Dramatic crimson sun, layered mountains and windy golden grass occupy the remaining backdrop. No grass over the mat or foreground obscuring cards.
Two large original card-shaped portraits: Doji Tatsuki on left, pale-haired Crane courtier in teal; Matsu Hachiro on right, red-armored Lion samurai. Preserve reference card-frame proportions and recognizable full printed card faces, NOT cropped character-only portraits. Cards stand nearly upright with only a slight backward lean, physically resting at their bottom edge on the mat, each about 34 percent of screen height. No easels or pedestals. Dominant, equally sized, readable faces.
CRITICAL attachment layout: TWO ATTACHMENT CARDS PER CHAMPION stand BEHIND their champion, vertically staggered upward in a restrained shallow staircase in DEPTH. Their complete top NAME BARS and upper ARTWORK bands are exposed above the champion so identity is readable at a glance. Minimal sideways offset, all three cards grouped in the champion's narrow silhouette. Do NOT fan attachment cards beside the champion. Show enough of each different attachment illustration to distinguish them.
Two clean rows of four smaller flat face-down focus cards, one row beneath each champion. Distinct physical Fate deck and discard piles near the outside left/right edges, kept entirely on the mat with border clearance. Local hand of five full cards in a shallow row at lower center, substantial enough to read when inspected, clear of border. Keep central crossed swords/five rings subtle and visible between champion groups.
Plain ivory dry-brush Musashi-style numerals “4” below Doji and “3” below Matsu, WITHOUT coins, badges or the word Chi. Small “Menu” top left. One strong ivory Musashi-style “STRIKE” with a restrained vermilion brush stroke, within unused bottom-right mat area. No bottom HUD strip, recap, aftermath panel, giant status ribbon, pile labels, counters, clan labels, VS text, explanatory copy, or hover inspector in this frame. Do not add human warriors outside the cards. Existing full-game inspection will be reused in implementation, not redesigned here.
Materials: navy woven campaign cloth with subtle aged stains, fine Japanese vine/chrysanthemum/wave gold edging, aged real card paper, realistic grounded shadows. Epic samurai-film visual tension with restrained UI. Front plane and upright cards sharp and readable; sunset softened slightly behind them. Respect gameplay legibility above cinematic haze.
layout_correction: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this L5R gameplay concept. Preserve camera, nearby navy mat, sunset, large upright champion cards, staggered attachment groups BEHIND each champion, hand, numbers, typography and gold border exactly. Two targeted card-pile corrections only: 1. Add a small separate physical FACE-UP Fate discard stack for each side in the free outer mat space directly BELOW its green face-down draw deck, to left of the left '4' and right of the right '3', above and clear of the bottom hand and Strike. Face-up discard must be distinct from the deck, not joined to it; readable visible top card, same flat mat perspective, no labels/counters. 2. Replace the eight dark tan custom-backed cards in the two focus rows with the SAME original GREEN five-rings card-back appearance as the two draw decks, maintaining their positions and sizes. Keep four per side. No new text, no HUD, no bottom recap, no card coins, no other changes.
opening:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: cinematic MOTION DESIGN STORYBOARD for the opening of an L5R Emperor Edition card duel. One beautiful contact sheet with FOUR sequential 16:9 game frames in a readable 2x2 grid, fine black gutters and discreet captions outside frames. Large landscape canvas with high detail.
Reference 1: the new closer-mat gameplay concept is the exact visual destination and visual language. Reference 2: user's champion-card reference preserves the identities, framed full-card faces, upright character cards. Keep every frame in the SAME red sunset field, navy Japanese campaign mat, aged gold filigree and full original printed cards.
Concept: “THE STILLNESS BEFORE THE DRAW”. Inspired by restrained samurai cinema: long stillness, lateral wind, deliberate close-ups, two equally formidable presences, then return to a readable card table. This is camera/light/card staging, not characters leaving their printed card art.
Frame 1 caption “01 · THE HUSH · 0.0–0.7s”: low close view across the front of the nearby navy mat toward the blood-red sun, two champion groups beginning to lift into upright position at left/right, windblown grass only outside the mat. Focus piles remain on the mat. Sparse, quiet, dramatic depth, nearly still.
Frame 2 caption “02 · THE CHALLENGER · 0.7–1.6s”: deliberate close-up of full upright Doji Tatsuki card, pale-haired teal-robed Crane; two attachment cards form a vertical staircase BEHIND her, exposed name bars and artwork above, NOT a sideways fan. Her exact name “DOJI TATSUKI” appears briefly in elegant ivory dry-brush Musashi-style heading with a small thin vermilion stroke. Other champion soft in distance, actual card face intact.
Frame 3 caption “03 · THE ANSWER · 1.6–2.5s”: matching equal-weight close-up of full upright Matsu Hachiro card, red-armored Lion, the same depth-staggered attachments behind, intact printed card face. Exact transient name “MATSU HACHIRO”, same brush typography and small vermilion accent. No permanent faction labels.
Frame 4 caption “04 · THE STANDOFF · 2.5–3.4s”: pull back only far enough to reveal the CLOSE playable mat filling the lower 72 percent of screen, both large upright framed champions equal in scale, attachment names/art readable behind them, simple brush “4” and “3”, flat deck/discard piles, clearly separated focus lanes, hand at near edge. Name overlays have dissolved. One small clear brush “STRIKE” on mat at bottom right. No bottom HUD or recap strip.
Materials and lighting: premium native game realism, warm sunset rim on paper edges, low charcoal shadows, navy cloth with fine floral/wave edging. Minimum particles, no fireworks, no glowing spell effects, no huge central VS, no DUEL title, no physical samurai figures, no coins, no bolts, no full-width menus. Maintain exact card identity and mat continuity across all frames. Visually intelligible sequence rather than four identical screenshots. Storyboard captures light and camera differences at the specified beats; captions outside the game image only.
ending:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: cinematic MOTION DESIGN STORYBOARD for a resolved L5R Emperor Edition duel, FOUR sequential 16:9 game frames in a 2x2 contact sheet with fine black gutters and discreet captions outside frames. Large landscape canvas, high detail.
Reference 1 is the exact closer-mat / upright-card gameplay target. Reference 2 establishes original full-frame Doji Tatsuki and Matsu Hachiro card identities. Reuse the red sunset field, navy Japanese filigree campaign mat, original card faces, attachments in a vertical depth staircase BEHIND champions, clear physical piles. Cards represent warriors; no extra embodied warriors.
Concept: “ONE STROKE, THEN SILENCE”. A samurai film's decisive release followed by the grave quiet of consequence, not celebratory fireworks. Depict the canonical demonstration where Doji Tatsuki wins 8 to 7. LEFT is Doji, RIGHT is Matsu throughout. Focus cards reveal only at the legal reveal moment.
Frame 1 caption “01 · THE REVEAL · 0.0–0.7s”: close gameplay view, focused cards turning face up in two readable lanes, plain ivory brush totals “8” on Doji's side and “7” on Matsu's. Main upright cards stay readable. Let the poised bilateral arrangement create suspense; no victory announced yet.
Frame 2 caption “02 · THE CUT · 0.7–0.9s”: same stable composition, a SINGLE brief restrained diagonal vermilion ink slash through the EMPTY space between the champions, a momentary darkened high-contrast stillness. Keep the faces and totals unobscured. No sword props flying, no beams or explosions, no blood spray and no damage painted across printed card faces.
Frame 3 caption “03 · THE CONSEQUENCE · 0.9–1.8s”: winner Doji remains upright and clearly lit. Matsu's physical card tilts down toward its own small separate fallen pile, his attachments move toward the appropriate distinct discard area, focused cards settle to Fate discards. Suggest motion only with restrained paper-edge ghosting. Preserve cards, no destruction into fragments. Numbers remain 8 left and 7 right. No misleading human body animation.
Frame 4 caption “04 · THE VERDICT · 1.8s–CONTINUE”: readable close mat in its final held state, upright full Doji card large at left, actual Matsu card rests visibly in separate fallen pile right with its name recognizable. No duplicate upright resurrected loser. Large restrained ivory dry-brush heading “DOJI TATSUKI WINS” centered over the quiet horizon; “8” and “7” remain side-aligned on the mat, winner numeral has short red ink underline. One compact “CONTINUE” in lower-right unused mat area. Keep a small unobtrusive “Details” text near Menu at upper left to retain optional consequence access. No bottom recap/footer/summary banner, no paragraphs, no coin, no faction placards.
The mood is solemn, earned, and decisive: warm rim light on victor, muted cooler shade on losing side, wind gradually returning. Premium cinematic game materials, quiet negative space, no confetti, no trophy icon, no exaggerated camera shake or white flash. The fourth frame is held for the player. Preserve same lens/layout identities across sequence.
opening_correction: Precise edit of this four-panel L5R opening storyboard. Preserve all four panels, captions, framing, sunset mood, upright full-card champions, original card faces and depth-staggered attachments, cinematic close-ups and brush names. Correct only the START-OF-DUEL card state: in ALL panels remove the small face-down committed focus cards on the mat, because neither player has focused at the opening. Retain the large physical green Fate draw-deck stacks at the outer edges and the separate face-up public discard piles. In the bottom-right gameplay panel, leave clean empty navy space between the two upright champions and the player's five-card hand where future focus cards will be placed; do not draw slot outlines, labels or empty placeholders. Retain 4 and 3 brush numerals, STRIKE, hand, and beautiful near mat. In top-left panel remove the small focus cards across the foreground only, keeping the two large deck stacks. All other pixels/design elements remain consistent. This is an opening animation BEFORE focus decisions, not a mid-duel screenshot.
ending_correction:
Precise edit of this FOUR-panel L5R victory storyboard. Preserve panels 1, 2 and 3, all captions, crimson sunset, mat material, fine gold border, large original champion cards, 8/7 totals, Musashi typography and the dramatic vermilion slash beat.
Correct ONLY the BOTTOM-RIGHT panel labeled “04 · THE VERDICT · 1.8s–CONTINUE” to show a properly SETTLED duel result:
- Keep Doji Tatsuki upright at left, with her own two attachments still visibly behind her, full face unaltered.
- Remove ALL eight revealed focus cards from the middle/lower mat; those focus lanes are now empty navy cloth. Both sides' resolved focus cards now form their own separate face-up FATE DISCARD stacks near the outer sides below the green Fate decks.
- At the RIGHT, Matsu Hachiro must lie FLAT on the mat as the top fully visible card of a SEPARATE small fallen-personality pile, physically distinct from the Fate discard. His card is no longer upright or tilted upward. Remove ALL translucent ghost cards or standing attachments from the right side.
- Matsu's former attachments belong in the right public discard area, so show them as flat cards in that stack, not sticking up behind his fallen personality. Keep draw deck, discard, and fallen pile distinct and spaced with mat-border padding.
- Retain side-aligned large plain 8 and 7, the small red underline under 8, the “DOJI TATSUKI WINS” heading, compact CONTINUE bottom-right, Menu/Details top-left. No bottom recap, paragraphs, coins, extra warriors, new graphics or empty slot outlines.
This final panel must feel quiet and resolved, with one standing victor and the aftermath represented by clear, separate physical piles. Only modify bottom-right panel.
